author: @FrankCurzio
text:
BREAKING: CoreWeave plans to borrow at least $4 billion at about half its junk bond rate.

Early talks point to 7% to 7.5%. Its existing bonds yield about 15%.

The new loan is backed by signed customer contracts, so lenders are really betting on CoreWeave's giant customers. Those customers are also prepaying about $9 billion. Nobody prepays for something that's easy to get.

That makes the buildout cheaper for CoreWeave ( $CRWV ) at $57.34, and the borrowed money ends up buying GPUs from Nvidia ( $NVDA ) at $158.64.

Interest costs still rose 173% in a year, a bit faster than sales.

But that gap between 15% and 7% is fear, and I'd still own CoreWeave here.

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
JUST IN: The world's biggest insurance broker wants the Fed to let banks hold less capital behind AI loans.

Marsh & McLennan $MMC is lobbying US regulators to ease the rules on loans covered by credit insurance.

Banks have lent so much to data center builders that they're running out of room. Right now, insuring a loan frees up NO capital for a US bank, but change that rule and a bank can insure the loan, free up its cushion & lend the money all over again.

Marsh gets a fee on every policy.

The risk doesn't go away. It just moves to insurers the public sees far less of, and some are already near their limits on data centers.

Banks pay for it too. Insurance can eat 50% to 70% of what they earn on the covered loans.

I've been negative on the big banks since March. This doesn't change it.

In 2008 everyone passed their risk to AIG. Whoever is left holding this AI risk takes the hit when the cycle turns.
media_note: photo related to insurance and AI loans

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
BREAKING: Drones just set one of Russia's two biggest Baltic oil ports on fire.

Three workers were hurt at Ust-Luga, the regional governor said. The port ships roughly 700,000 barrels of oil a day.

On Monday it was a refinery. Now Ukraine is hitting the place Russia sells its oil from, and that export money pays for the war (right before US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi this week).

Brent fell below $90 on hopes the Iran war ends, and Trump calls Abu Dhabi a chance for a breakthrough. Oil under $90 assumes two wars end at once.

A deal doesn't fix a burned terminal.

Chevron is moving drilling money to places no drone can reach, and services companies like Halliburton get paid to do that work.

I'd rather own the companies drilling far from every war zone.

author: @BearBullTraders
text: As @elonmusk once said, “If she’s a 10, you’re an asset!”
quoted_text:
$NVDA’s CEO Jensen Huang just admitted to an affair and US officials reportedly believe the woman was working for Chinese intelligence!

Nvidia shares fell as much as 8% after the news broke. The board says there's no sign any secrets were leaked and China calls the spy claims slander. 

@elonmusk : "If she's a 10, you're an asset" line isn't new, by the way. He tweeted it last October, when the honeypot reports first came out.

Nvidia spends billions keeping hackers out and now it's learning the cheapest way in was never code.

Keep that Huang to yourself!
